name: advancecomp
why: Aggressively recompresses PNG and ZIP files with better deflate; a fun look at how file containers can be squeezed further.

brief.what_it_is: AdvanceCOMP is a set of command-line recompression utilities for .ZIP archives, .PNG images, .MNG video clips and .GZ files. It takes an existing compressed file and rewrites it with a stronger deflate encoder, so the file stays valid but gets smaller. The package ships four executables: advzip (zip files), advpng (png files), advmng (mng files) and advdef (deflate streams inside png, mng and gz files).
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it is mainly intended for recompressing a collection of emulated-game rom, snapshot and clip files.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says it recompresses ZIP, GZ, PNG and MNG files using the Deflate 7-Zip implementation, and recompresses MNG files using Delta and Move optimization. The README gives no further detail on the mechanism.
brief.install_notes: The fetched pages give no install steps beyond the Homebrew formula name. The GitHub README says the package runs on Linux, Mac OS X, DOS, Windows and other Unix-like platforms. No runtime, account or configuration is mentioned.
brief.standout: Rather than a new compressor, it re-encodes the deflate streams inside existing containers (ZIP, PNG, GZ, MNG) with the 7-Zip deflate implementation, so the output stays a standard file. The homepage also points users to OptiPNG and pngcrush as other PNG optimizers.
brief.status: Unknown. The fetched homepage and GitHub README show no release date, last commit date or version number, so I cannot judge whether it is actively maintained. The homepage does link to a download page, a forum and a support page, which I did not fetch.
brief.caveats: The fetched pages list no command-line usage, so I could not confirm flags or invocation syntax. The homepage says the tool is mainly aimed at emulation rom and snapshot collections. The homepage names other PNG optimizers (OptiPNG, pngcrush) as alternatives, which suggests the project is not a general-purpose PNG optimizer. The Homebrew entry has no caveats.
